Subject: Request: penetration report and exec synopsis for SOC2 audit

Hi Vanessa,

We are starting our SOC 2 Type II evidence collection and our audit team has asked for a recent penetration test and an executive synopsis that we can attach to the evidence packet. For audit purposes we need enough detail to demonstrate that findings were identified, tracked, and remediated (or a plan exists).

Before we proceed, two asks:
- Can Redwood share an executive summary (redacted as needed) now?
- For the full pen test report, would Redwood be willing to provide access via an escrow/secure-transfer (time-boxed) under a mutual NDA so our audit firm can review the details?

If there are standard redaction rules or a deliverable playbook you prefer we follow, please share. Our ideal timeline is to have the exec summary by Jun 7 and secured access to the full report by Jun 14.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Ruth Alvarez
Head of Security Assurance
FinServe Inc.

Ruth — thanks for the clear asks and timelines. We can support this, but we need to align legal and our security remediation team on the exchange specifics.

Quick summary of our approach (proposal):
1) Provide a redacted executive summary (PDF) with a redaction matrix indicating which sections were sanitized.
2) Deliver the full encrypted report to a third-party escrow vendor (time-limited, one-time access) after a mutual NDA is executed.
3) Provide a remediation log showing status and dates for high/critical items (we can sample items for your auditors).

Kimberly (Legal) — can you review and propose minimal redaction rules and whether an escrow + mutual NDA works from Redwood's side?
Aditya (Security) — can you prepare a remediation status snapshot for the requested window and flag any embargoed details that must remain internal?

Proposed next steps: Kimberly to send a redlineable playbook by end of day tomorrow; I will share a draft exec summary once we have that.

Hi all — looping in Legal on the suggested exchange model. Attaching a first draft redaction playbook for comment. Key points from our side: 

- We will produce an executive summary limited to findings, business impact, and high-level remediation actions. We will redact: PoC code, exact exploit steps, internal IPs/hostnames, and details that would enable exploitation (sample redaction examples in the doc).
- For the full report: we can transfer an encrypted package to a third-party escrow provider (we currently use ThirdParty-Escrow) that supports time-limited, audited access and per-file watermarking. Access will require a signed mutual NDA and an access request form from the auditor.
- Escrow access window: standard is 72 hours after approval; we can extend to 7 days on request with justification.
- Verification: we will provide a remediation matrix (CVE/ID, status, patch date) for items labeled High/Critical. We recommend the auditor validate a sample of 3–5 items, not the entire report, to balance audit requirements and risk.

Attachments: redaction_playbook_draft.docx, nda-redline-finserve.pdf

Please review and mark changes in the docx if you need narrower/wider redaction. Ruth — if your auditor needs different acceptance criteria for remediation validation, flag that and we can adapt.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
